value.rationale: The target paper repeatedly evaluates stress–strength reliability numerically and bases simulations, plug-in estimators, and applications on that series. The finding replaces a local heuristic with a rigorous closed-form error certificate and shows, on one of the paper's own parameter scenarios, that the printed 10^{-6} rule can understate the actual truncation error by more than three orders of magnitude. This directly affects reproducible numerical reliability evaluation rather than merely refining notation.
